item.description:
Correction | Procurement | Award | $53K | Vendor: Insparisk LLC

This is a requirements contract to furnish all labor, materials, tools, and equipment as necessary to provide periodic third party witness services and inspection services for various types of elevators, dumbwaiters, mechanical lifts, related machinery, shafts, and other devices henceforth stated as devices as directed by New York City Department of Correction (DOC). item.title: Board of Correction Public Meeting
item.description:
Board of Correction | Public Hearings and Meetings | Meeting | Hearing: 2026-06-09

The New York City Board of Correction will hold a public meeting on Tuesday, June 9, 2026 at 1:00pm. The meeting with be held in the auditorium located on the 2nd floor of 125 Worth Street. The Board will discuss issues impacting the New York City jail system.

More information is available on the Board's website at https://www.nyc.gov/site/boc/meetings/2026-meetings.page

  • Wheelchair Access. The venue has an accessible entrance on Lafayette Street and elevators. There are accessible bathrooms on the first floor of the building.

item.title: Programmable Logic Controller (PLC)
item.description:
Correction | Procurement | Award | $330K | Vendor: Tomex Electronics Inc

The New York City Department of Correction (NYCDOC) seeks a qualified M/WBE-certified vendor to develop and implement a comprehensive integration of the Departments existing Programmable Logic Controller (PLC)based jail control panels with the Genetec Security Center platform. The project encompasses two independent cell wings, each containing 48 inmate cells and 4 auxiliary rooms (totaling 104 access points across both wings). Each wing operates using its own PLC hardware and wiring infrastructure, which must be integrated into DOCs unified Genetec security ecosystem for centralized command, monitoring, automation, and video-assisted situational awareness. This modernization initiative aims to replace manual, panel-based workflows with automated, rules-driven functionality, enhancing operator efficiency, reducing human error, and improving DOCs ability to escalate, track, and respond to security-critical events in real time

item.title: Inmate Communication Services - NAE
item.description:
Correction | Procurement | Award | $3.9M | Vendor: Securus Technologies LLC

In accordance with section 3-04(b)(2)(iii) of the NYC Procurement Policy Rules, DOC intends to enter into a Negotiated Acquisition Extension with Securus Technologies for an additional 6 months, starting approximately January 1, 2026 through June 30, 2026 to avoid disruption in inmate communication and tablet-based services and to also ensure continuity of service while the Department finalize the replacement procurement via an RFP.
